summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with severe aortic stenosis, diastolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was readmitted for worsening shortness of breath and 5-pound weight gain, indicating acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation. He was treated with intravenous furosemide, transitioned to oral torsemide 20 mg daily, and underwent a right thoracentesis that removed 3.5 liters of transudative fluid, significantly improving his breathing. His hyponatremia and acute kidney injury resolved with diuresis. Warfarin was held temporarily due to bleeding risk, and metoprolol was increased to 150 mg daily for rate control. A multidisciplinary discussion concluded that valve intervention was not beneficial. He was discharged home with home health services, on strict fluid and sodium restrictions, with instructions to monitor daily weights and follow up for INR checks and symptom management.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Other dependence on machines, supplemental oxygen
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
